The '''2026 Harrow London Borough Council election''' took place on 7 May 2026. All 55 members of [[Harrow London Borough Council]] were elected. The elections took place alongside other [[2026 United Kingdom local elections]], including [[2026 London local elections|local elections in the other 31 London boroughs.]]

== Background ==
London borough councils are the principal authorities in [[Greater London]] and have responsibilities including education, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health, housing development and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]] and the [[Mayor of London]], which also manage passenger transport, police and fire.

Harrow voted in a Conservative council in its first election in 1964, and (excluding a brief three-year period of no overall control) Harrow remained Conservative-controlled till 1994. In that year, the Liberal Democrats became the biggest party on the council, although the council had no overall control. In 1998, Labour won a majority on Harrow Council for the first time.

Labour lost their majority in 2002 and the Tories retook the council in 2006, only to lose it to Labour again in 2010. Although there was a brief period of no overall control, Labour won majorities in [[2014 Harrow London Borough Council election|2014]] and [[2018 Harrow London Borough Council election|2018]].

In [[2022 Harrow London Borough Council election|2022]], the Conservatives won a majority on Harrow Council, with 31 seats, while Labour were reduced to 24,<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 May 2022 |title=Election results by party, 5 May 2022 – Harrow Council |url=https://moderngov.harrow.gov.uk/mgElectionResults.aspx?ID=44&RPID=155628722 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520142243/https://moderngov.harrow.gov.uk/mgElectionResults.aspx?ID=44&RPID=155628722 |archive-date=20 May 2022 |access-date=12 December 2025 |website=Harrow Council |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> defeating the incumbent Labour administration of twelve years, which had held a majority for eight of those years.

Both the Tories and Labour stood 55 candidates each in 2022, while the Liberal Democrats stood 28 candidates, Greens stood 14 candidates, and Reform stood 3 candidates. 9 candidates stood as independents.
[[File:Harrow UK local election 2022 map.svg|thumb|243x243px|The Conservatives took control of Harrow Council from Labour in 2022]]
In June 2023, Labour suspended a councillor, Phillip O'Dell, who became an independent.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 June 2023 |title=Harrow councillor has whip removed during investigation - but no details given |url=https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/23562904.harrow-councillor-phillip-odell-labour-whip-removed/ |access-date=12 December 2025 |website=Harrow Times |language=en}}</ref> That same year, Mayor of London, [[Sadiq Khan]], expanded the [[Ultra Low Emission Zone|Ultra-Low Emission Zone]] to outer London (ULEZ). This was challenged in court by [[Bexley London Borough Council|Bexley]], [[Bromley London Borough Council|Bromley]], Harrow and [[Hillingdon London Borough Council|Hillingdon]] councils, although the court challenge was defeated.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Landmark High Court win for Mayor means ULEZ expansion will go ahead {{!}} London City Hall |url=https://www.london.gov.uk/landmark-high-court-win-mayor-means-ulez-expansion-will-go-ahead |access-date=14 December 2025 |website=www.london.gov.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref>

On 4 July 2024, the [[2024 United Kingdom general election]] saw a Labour Party victory, with a total 411 seats. The Conservative Party saw a reduction in their total seats to 121, the lowest in their history, resulting in [[Keir Starmer]] becoming Prime Minister. However, Labour had won this landslide on less than 35 percent of the vote, and a rapid collapse in Labour (and also Conservative) polling combined with the surge of Reform UK, has led to some political commentators suggesting that the two-party system has ended or has come close to ending.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The end of the two-party system? What the experts are saying about the 2025 local elections |url=https://electoral-reform.org.uk/the-end-of-the-two-party-system-what-the-experts-are-saying-about-the-2025-local-elections/ |access-date=14 December 2025 |website=electoral-reform.org.uk |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Papazoglou |first=Alexis |date=13 May 2025 |title=The two-party system may finally be breaking {{!}} British Politics and Policy at LSE |url=https://blogs.lse.ac.uk/politicsandpolicy/the-two-party-system-may-finally-be-breaking/ |access-date=14 December 2025 |website=British Politics and Policy at LSE {{!}}}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Beckett |first=Andy |date=6 November 2025 |title=Britain's two-party politics is fragmenting: what unintended consequences await? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2025/nov/06/britain-two-party-politics-unintended-consequences |access-date=14 December 2025 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>
[[File:Council control of the London Borough of Harrow before the 2026 election.png|thumb|Council control of the London Borough of Harrow in 2022. The black line represents the majority line.]]
A new party, Arise, was formed in August 2025 with the backing of [[Jeremy Corbyn]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=10 December 2025 |title=New political party backed by Corbyn launches campaign in Harrow |url=https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/25686721.jeremy-corbyn-endorsed-party-launches-campaign-harrow/ |access-date=12 December 2025 |website=Harrow Times |language=en}}</ref> This party is led by Pamela Fitzpatrick,<ref name=":0" /> a Labour councillor between 2014 and 2021, then an independent councillor until 2022, and an independent candidate for Harrow West in the 2024 general election. They have announced that they intend to target [[Marlborough (ward)|Marlborough ward]].

== Council administration ==
In 2025, ''Harrow Times'' reported that the Conservative council invested £3 million into renovating council housing.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 September 2025 |title=£3m spent by council to install brand new kitchens and bathrooms |url=https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/25461115.harrow-council-spends-3m-new-kitchens-bathrooms/ |access-date=2 April 2026 |website=Harrow Times |language=en}}</ref>

In 2026, the Conservatives increased Harrow council tax by 4.99%. Labour leader David Perry called the budget a "disaster for this Conservative administration," and claimed the Tories "voted to break their own election promises by raising council tax by the maximum 5 per cent for a fourth consecutive year."<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 March 2026 |title=Harrow Council tax rising by maximum rate from next month - but what's it paying for? |url=https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/25920989.harrow-residents-council-tax-rise-maximum-4-99/ |access-date=16 March 2026 |website=Harrow Times |language=en}}</ref> Harrow also has the third-highest council tax in London, having dropped down from the second-highest rate under the previous Labour administration at the 2022 election, which was run by Roxbourne councillor Graham Henson. The two councils that pay more council tax than Harrow are Lib Dem-run [[Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames|Kingston-upon-Thames]] and Conservative-run [[London Borough of Croydon|Croydon]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporter) |first=Noah Vickers (Local Democracy |date=21 March 2024 |title=Harrow ranks third for highest average council tax bill in London, over £2,200 per year |url=https://harrowonline.org/2024/03/21/harrow-ranks-third-for-highest-average-council-tax-bill-in-london-over-2200-per-year/ |access-date=23 March 2026 |website=Harrow Online |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Jones |first=Ian |title=Council tax rates 2022/23 in your area - see how much you will pay as average bill hits £1,966 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/council-tax-how-much-pay-b2047205.html |work=The Independent |date=30 March 2022 |access-date=19 April 2026}}</ref>

== Electoral system ==
London borough councils elect all of their councillors at once every four years. The previous election took place in 2022. The election will take place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors will have as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected, depending on the ward.

28 seats are needed for a majority on Harrow Council. Prior to the election, Conservatives had a majority<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=London Borough of Harrow |date=5 May 2022 |title=Election results by wards |url=https://moderngov.harrow.gov.uk/mgElectionElectionAreaResults.aspx?EID=44&RPID=271328721 |website=London Borough of Harrow}}</ref> and Labour needed an increase of 4 seats to gain a majority. The narrowest Labour defeats in 2022 were North Harrow, by 5 votes, Rayners Lane, by 15 votes, North Harrow, by 39 votes, and Edgware, by 49 votes.<ref name=":1" /> (North Harrow and Rayners Lane each have two councillors and Edgware has three.) 

== Policies ==
The Harrow [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] have campaigned on their record leading the council, promising to protect one-hour free parking, crack down on [[House in multiple occupation|houses in multiple occupation]] (HMOs),<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 January 2026 |title=Cracking down on conversions of family homes to HMOs |url=https://www.harrowconservatives.com/news/cracking-down-conversions-family-homes-hmos |access-date=19 April 2026 |website=Harrow |language=en}}</ref> resist overdevelopment in the [[Green belt (United Kingdom)|green belt]], prosecute fly-tipping and maintain clean streets, invest more in road resurfacing and repairs, and protect the [[Freedom Pass]] and [[Winter Fuel Payment|Winter Fuel Payments]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite news |last=Grant Williams (Local Democracy Reporter) |date=20 April 2026 |title=Harrow election 2026: what each party is promising – and who's tipped to win - Harrow Online |url=https://harrowonline.org/2026/04/20/harrow-election-2026-what-each-party-is-promising-and-whos-tipped-to-win/ |access-date=6 May 2026 |work=Harrow Online |language=en-US}}</ref>

Harrow [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] has campaigned on six "key pledges", promising to freeze [[Council Tax]] in 2027, offer one-hour free parking, double residential cleaning to every two weeks, create an anti-social behaviour squad, introduce tougher penalties for fly-tippers and a private alleyway clearance scheme, and crack down on HMOs and rogue landlords.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 April 2026 |title=Labour vows to freeze council tax and reverse cuts to essential services |url=https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/26004738.harrow-council-opposition-leader-reasons-vote-labour/ |access-date=18 April 2026 |website=Harrow Times |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=toby.poole@harrow.gov.uk |date=8 April 2026 |title=Harrow Labour - 6 Key Pledges |url=https://www.harrowlabour.co.uk/2026/04/08/harrow-labour-6-key-pledges/ |access-date=19 April 2026 |website=Harrow Labour Group |language=en-US}}</ref>

The Harrow [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] published a manifesto promising to improve waste management standards to reduce littering, build affordable homes that are built sustainably, make Harrow attractive for business, get an 'Outstanding' [[Ofsted]] rating for council-provided children's services, improve contacting the council, and make improvements to roads with an emphasis on active travel and safety.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2026 Election Manifesto - Harrow Liberal Democrats |url=https://www.harrowlibdems.org.uk/campaigns/2026-election-manifesto |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=www.harrowlibdems.org.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref name=":6" />

The Harrow [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] listed their priorities for Harrow as: improving access to [[General practitioner|GP]] services and supporting local schools, cracking down on bad landlords and raising standards for tenants, fixing poor housing and pushing for more affordable and accessible homes, cleaning up streets and tackling fly-tipping, protecting nature and biodiversity, protecting green spaces and making them safer, cleaning up rivers, supporting community wellbeing and local services, celebrating Harrow’s diversity and bringing communities together, and making the council more open, accountable and responsive.<ref>{{Cite web |last=alexanderlee |date=18 April 2026 |title=A greener, fairer Harrow – Local Elections May 2026 |url=https://harrow.greenparty.org.uk/2026/04/18/a-greener-fairer-harrow-local-elections-may-2026/ |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=Harrow Green Party |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":6" />

[[Reform UK]] Harrow has promised to: tackle crime, drug dealing, antisocial behaviour and street drinking; protect one-hour free parking; stop overdevelopment and unlicensed HMOs; focus on repairing potholes to fix roads; make town centre improvements; and take public health seriously on spitting and tuberculosis.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Reform UK Harrow |date=16 April 2026 |title=REFORM UK HARROW MANIFESTO #ReformUK #Harrow #London #politics #hope #timeforchange #TimeForHarrow #Manifesto |url=https://x.com/HarrowReformUK/status/2044847513249730914 |website=X}}</ref><ref name=":6" />

Arise Harrow listed the issues of housing, education and [[Special Educational Needs|SEN]] provision, poverty, community spaces, disability rights, social care, and having an ethical council as its priorities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arise Party {{!}} New Harrow-Based Political Party |url=https://ariseparty.org.uk/ |access-date=6 May 2026 |language=en|website=Arise Party|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260506125517/https://ariseparty.org.uk/|archive-date=6 May 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Arise pledged to: stop the conversion of family homes into overcrowded HMOs, strengthen enforcement against rogue landlords, provide affordable homes by building council housing, investigate the high rate of school exclusions, ensure every child has a suitable school place, bring care homes under council control, introduce free adult social care at home with [[Meals on Wheels|meals on wheels]]; create a not-for-profit community supermarket, divest the council from companies involved in human rights violations, such as in Palestine, Congo, and South Sudan, and repurpose empty buildings into community spaces.<ref name=":6" />

26 candidates signed the [[Palestine Solidarity Campaign]]'s 'Candidate Pledge for Palestine', pledging to "uphold the rights of the Palestinian people, stand up to Israel for its crimes of [[Gaza genocide|genocide]] and [[Israeli apartheid|apartheid]], and ensure their councils are not complicit, including through [[Divestment from Israel|divestment]] of pension funds from complicit companies".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Magee |first=Caolán |title=More than 1,000 UK councillors sign Palestine pledge as local polls loom |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/26/more-than-1000-uk-councillors-sign-pledge-as-local-polls-loom |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=Candidate Pledge for Palestine |url=https://palestinecampaign.org/candidate-pledge-for-palestine/ |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=Palestine Solidarity Campaign |language=en-GB}}</ref> This includes 12 Green candidates, 11 Arise candidates, and 3 Labour candidates.<ref name=":8" />
